narrative:
The model estimates a 51% chance that you will leave your current job, which is just over the threshold for predicting departure. As a result, the organization has decided to deny your promotion.

The prediction is driven primarily by three key factors in your profile. First, having only 1-5 years of total professional experience across all roles was the strongest influence pulling the prediction toward leaving. Among employees the model expected to stay, half still fall in this early-career bracket, yet the model sees limited overall experience as a notable risk for turnover. Second, the fact that you have received other job offers while working here pushed the prediction further toward leaving, as external opportunities often signal higher likelihood of departure. Finally, your high emotional commitment to the organization worked in the opposite direction, pulling the prediction back toward staying and helping to moderate the risk.

Taken together, your relatively short overall experience and the presence of outside offers outweighed the protective effect of your strong emotional attachment, tipping the model just past the 50% mark.

The organization should consider discussing your career progression and external opportunities with you openly. You may wish to reflect on whether additional experience, clearer advancement paths, or addressing any unmet needs could change your outlook before making a decision.
